findings.baseline_finding: Cleanup could close shared public descriptors while admitted submissions still prepared or launched roles; descriptor reuse could cross the intended owner-only candidate boundary.
findings.closure: Both Popen admission sites and submission admission use the shared closing lock. Finish closes admission atomically. Abort blocks later admission, stops and reaps registered processes, waits for active submissions to quiesce, then closes shared descriptors and the journal. Active markers clear even when journaling fails.

findings.baseline_finding: A global journal-consumer error marker was ignored by role waiters, allowing an indefinite wait while the dependency process remained live.
findings.closure: Direct journal and consumer errors set a terminal failure and notify the condition. Waiters check that failure before cached status values and raise into cleanup.
